import { Callout } from 'fumadocs-ui/components/callout';

[`fiber-checkout`](https://github.com/salmansarwarr/Fiber-checkout) is a
community-maintained React library for invoice-based Fiber checkout flows. It
can create an invoice, render its QR code, poll the invoice status, detect
expiry, and report payment success through one component or lower-level hooks.

<Callout type="warning" title="Compatibility and support">
  `fiber-checkout` is a community project delivered through the Spark Program
  and is now in stable maintenance. Its published peer dependency targets
  `@nervosnetwork/fiber-js` v0.7.x, while Fiber continues to evolve. Verify the
  current upstream compatibility notes and test your exact Fiber Node version
  before production use.
</Callout>

## When to use it

Use `fiber-checkout` when a merchant or service needs to **receive** a Fiber
payment with a ready-made React checkout. If you need a browser-local node,
passkey wallet, channel management, or a broader RPC client, consider
[fiber-pay](/docs/build/community-sdk/fiber-pay) or the
[JavaScript SDK](/docs/build/sdk/js) instead.

## Install

```bash
npm install fiber-checkout
```

The package supports React 18 and 19. Its RPC-only mode does not require the
Fiber WASM runtime.

## Add a checkout component

```tsx
import { FiberCheckout, ckbToShannonHex } from "fiber-checkout";

export default function CheckoutPage() {
  return (
    <FiberCheckout
      amount={ckbToShannonHex(1)}
      asset="CKB"
      nodeUrl="/api/fiber-rpc"
      description="Order #1234"
      onSuccess={(paymentHash) => {
        console.log("Payment confirmed:", paymentHash);
      }}
      onExpired={() => console.log("Invoice expired")}
      onError={(error) => console.error(error.code, error.message)}
    />
  );
}
```

The component uses `new_invoice` to create the invoice and `get_invoice` to
observe its status. For a custom UI, the package also exports
`useFiberInvoice()` and `useFiberPayment()`.

## Put an RPC proxy in front of your node

In production, do not expose a Fiber node RPC endpoint directly to browsers.
Route checkout requests through a server endpoint that:

- keeps the node address and credentials on the server;
- accepts only the RPC methods required by the checkout;
- applies your authentication, rate limits, and request validation; and
- serves the public application over HTTPS without browser CORS or mixed-content
  failures.

The expected request path is:

```text
Browser -> your HTTPS RPC proxy -> your Fiber node
```

At minimum, allow only `new_invoice` and `get_invoice` for this checkout flow.
Validate the JSON-RPC payload before forwarding it instead of passing arbitrary
methods and parameters to the node.

<Callout type="warning" title="Direct RPC is for local development only">
  The `dangerouslyAllowDirectRpc` option is intended for a trusted local setup.
  Enabling it in production exposes the node RPC surface and its network address
  to every browser user.
</Callout>

## Assets and WASM mode

The built-in component accepts CKB and RUSD and can be extended with a custom
asset registry. Confirm every UDT type script against the issuer's official
deployment before accepting payment.

If an application already runs a browser node with
`@nervosnetwork/fiber-js`, `FiberWasmBackend` can reuse that instance instead of
calling a remote RPC proxy. Review the upstream peer-dependency and Fiber Node
compatibility before choosing this mode.
